No existing relief is terminated, pending motion decided or disputed temporal application resolved by admission alone. [Source](../entering-law/PUBLIC_Prison_Litigation_Reform_Act_sections_802_804_statutory_enactment_1996-04-26.md). |

## Published noncontrolling positions


Earlier published positions retain their scope under the opening trackers. A successor does not inherit a retired Justice’s position. The positions below are noncontrolling unless a later identified Court holding adopts them.

### Doe v Taylor ISD — 1995-10-16

**Stone-Zsela, concurring in the Caplinger judgment.** The Chief Justice joins Parts I and II but would resolve Caplinger’s component on the merits. Each official must be assessed on his own information and response. Caplinger’s later and more limited information, inquiries, interview and warnings, despite their alleged deficiencies, do not amount on the assumed facts to the knowing disregard potentially shown against Lankford. The date of notice alone is no excuse; the decisive distinction is personal culpability. The Chief Justice does not rely on the absence of close precedent, impute the principal’s knowledge, resolve the January/February conflict, or establish a general right to an adequate school investigation. This ground is not the Court’s Caplinger holding.

**O’Connor, joined by Scalia, Kennedy, and Thomas, concurring in part and dissenting in part.** These Justices join the legal/factual review boundary and Caplinger’s immunity, but would grant Lankford immunity too. Ingraham’s bodily-security principle and the teacher’s obvious wrong do not by themselves settle the separate supervisor’s constitutional obligation during 1986–1987. The contemporary cases distinguished personal action, policy, affirmative linkage and omissions, and often rejected the asserted supervisory liability. Hafer’s personal-responsibility rule and Elder’s complete review do not eliminate that specificity problem. Farmer and other later formulations cannot provide retrospective notice. The dissent assumes the pleaded facts for this legal inquiry; it neither endorses abuse nor holds that every omission is beyond §1983.

Authority and exact joins: [Public decision](../entering-law/PUBLIC_Doe_v_Taylor_ISD_merits_1995-10-16.md).

### Hodge v Jones — 1995-10-23

**Stone-Zsela, concurring in part and in the judgment.** The Chief Justice joins the prospective mootness holding but would reject the damages claim because the asserted constitutional deprivation is absent on this record. The State may retain an accurate, confidential account of a legitimate investigation; a report recording clearance is not a finding of parental dangerousness. No separation, public disclosure, particular family interference or legal disability is established. Roth and Olim distinguish state procedure from a substantive federal entitlement, so a claimed procedural departure alone is insufficient. This ground is limited to the preserved report and injuries. It does not approve knowingly false records, retention contrary to an enforceable substantive right, broad dissemination, or automatic family restrictions, and does not deny all constitutional protection to intimate information. The Chief Justice does not rest on lack of close precedent. His merits conclusion is not the Court’s holding.

Authority and exact joins: [Public decision](../entering-law/PUBLIC_Hodge_v_Jones_merits_1995-10-23.md).

### Tuggle v Netherland — 1995-10-30

**Stone-Zsela, concurring; O'Connor and Souter join only the proposed Chapman rule for a preserved, properly available capital-sentencing denial of required psychiatric assistance when the State presents psychiatric future-danger evidence.** The Chief Justice joins the Court because its surviving-aggravator ground independently requires vacatur whatever error-effect standard ultimately governs. He would also extend O'Neal to an available Ake denial of this kind: the State must establish beyond a reasonable doubt on the whole penalty record that the denial did not contribute to the death sentence. O'Connor and Souter support that proposal within the preserved and properly available category just described; their joins do not extend to the Chief Justice's further remedial directions.

A psychiatric defense serves investigation, cross-examination, rebuttal, and mitigation. An unrebutted future-danger case can influence the whole sentencing choice after its aggravator is removed. The State's asserted evidentiary advantage arises from the very denial that makes the missing defense difficult to reconstruct; the defendant should not bear that uncertainty. This is a proposed extension, not a claim that O'Neal already governs all Ake errors. A surviving eligibility finding cannot replace examination of whether the decision to impose death was constitutionally reliable.

The Chief Justice assumes the 1985 penalty-stage violation for this review without relying on the withdrawn concession. Any renewed request or threshold challenge must be available under the existing rulings and preservation rules. If the violation stands, he would require review of the whole penalty record, including what competent assistance could have supplied for rebuttal and mitigation, without inventing testimony. If harmless under the governing standard, relief on this error should be denied; otherwise he would require a conditional writ allowing a constitutionally adequate new penalty proceeding within a reasonable District Court deadline or replacement of the death sentence by lawful relief. No deadline is fixed now. If the present submissions have not addressed the governing standard, he would permit briefing, including on his proposed Chapman extension. He would not order a new hearing now, declare harmlessness, classify the error as structural, order a guilt retrial, or decide an independent state-aggravator issue. These further directions are his own; the Court reserves the applicable standard and ultimate relief.

Authority and exact joins: [Public decision](../entering-law/PUBLIC_Tuggle_v_Netherland_summary_merits_1995-10-30.md).

### Libretti v United States — 1995-11-07

**Stone-Zsela, concurring in the judgment and joining Part I-B.** The Chief Justice upholds Libretti's informed relinquishment of a forfeiture jury and leaves the right's constitutional source unresolved. A sentencing label alone cannot answer the constitutional question, and the actual waiver makes an answer unnecessary. Gaudin remains the rule for enacted elements; this disposition neither expands nor displaces it.

Section 853 fixes the court's power to take property. Actual admissions and existing evidence can establish that basis without another hearing for every item, but a promise to forfeit cannot authorize an otherwise forbidden sentence. Lawful source alone is not immunity where the property is an instrumentality, an enterprise interest or authorized substitute property. The existing orders, admissions and evidence support rejecting a wholesale new proceeding on the reviewed claims; those claims do not establish an identified, still-operative defendant-owned portion requiring vacatur. That is not a finding that every § 853(p) predicate was proved for every item or an endorsement of forfeiture by agreement alone. A demonstrated statutory defect in an identified portion would require its vacatur and lawful separation or further treatment; no prior final invalidity judgment would be necessary. The April adverse findings, effective third-party returns and defendant-specific postappeal jurisdiction limit retain their exact scope. The check, IRA and Porter claim remain distinct, and no conditional pension exclusion is applied without its predicate. Supported portions, the guilty plea and conviction are preserved.

**Souter, concurring in part and in the judgment.** Justice Souter joins Parts I-A, I-B and III. He agrees that the right must be understood before it can be surrendered and resolves the case without deciding its constitutional source. Ordinary jury advice, understood with an indictment's forfeiture allegation, can cover the charged forfeiture question without reciting a rule number. Advice affirmatively suggesting that the jury right excludes forfeiture would present a different problem. The two earlier references to the jury's forfeiture function answer the possible misleading implication of the later guilt-focused explanation here; represented assent and the express end of trial then establish surrender. Godinez and Olano preserve that actual-choice requirement. He does not join the five's constitutional classification or broader sufficient-waiver formulation, require an automatic additional hearing, or infer private advice absent from the record.

**Ginsburg, concurring in part and in the judgment.** Justice Ginsburg joins Parts I-A, I-B and III. She requires awareness of the unusual forfeiture special-verdict right, and relies on the pretrial references to that jury function followed by Libretti's represented agreement and express assent to ending trial. A bare reading of a forfeiture allegation or broad signature need not suffice in another case. An explicit plea-hearing explanation is a readily available protection, but the omission of that additional warning does not require remand when the record otherwise establishes informed relinquishment. The limited Mezzanatto consent principle supports attention to the protection actually surrendered. She leaves the constitutional source unresolved and withholds the broader formulation in Part II; she neither finds a constitutional jury right nor equates statutory classification with knowing waiver.

**Stevens, dissenting, while joining Parts I-A and I-B.** Justice Stevens agrees that Rule 11(f) does not impose the requested forfeiture inquiry and that a known jury right may be surrendered. His dissent instead requires the sentencing court independently to assure itself that its punishment stays within § 853 where the record raises a concrete question about the forfeiture order's breadth. Bigelow and Ex parte Lange distinguish punishment exceeding statutory power from an arguably erroneous exercise of lawful power; Roberts illustrates why agreement alone cannot make an item forfeitable. A broad all-assets bargain cannot purchase authority Congress withheld.

The record supports portions of the order and expressly designates a substitute check. Those facts do not by themselves establish the basis for every additional interest embraced by the appellate all-assets rationale. The April court's affirmative adverse findings and its attempted defendant-specific further inquiry reinforce the distinction between assent and authority, even though the defendant's pending appeal defeated that reopening. Stevens would vacate the defendant's forfeiture disposition and remand for the statutory assurance he finds missing. He does not declare the check, IRA, Wyochem balance or every asset invalid, erase third-party orders or require automatic return. He leaves the constitutional question unresolved and does not premise remand on a finding of ignorance despite the jury notices. The remand would not automatically rescind guilt or preserve every benefit of a sentence-contingent bargain: if the court rejected an agreement governed by former Rule 11(e)(1)(C), Rule 11(e)(4)'s opportunity to withdraw would apply. That condition is not established merely by the existence of this forfeiture agreement.

Authority and exact joins: [Public decision](../entering-law/PUBLIC_Libretti_v_United_States_merits_1995-11-07.md).

### American Life League v Reno — 1995-11-13

**O'Connor, joined by Souter, concurring in part.** They join the rejection of demonstrated facial targeting, the commerce and speech holdings and the RFRA remand. They do not join Part V-B's broader constitutional rejection under Smith. Their respective Lukumi positions preserve the substantial-burden constitutional question and reconsideration of Smith's foundation; the statutory remand makes its resolution unnecessary here. They recognize the own-minor exception's actual limits and do not create a constitutional exemption, invalidate FACE or dispute the present facial constitutional disposition. Their RFRA inquiry leaves open a justified denial of an exemption on a sufficient claimant-specific showing.

**Stone-Zsela, joined by Stevens, Ginsburg and Breyer, dissenting in part.** They accept Clearwater and Swanner as governing and would affirm the RFRA dismissal on the pleaded assumption that religious exercise requires the defined physical obstruction. Their disagreement concerns whether that application already supplies sufficient justification, not RFRA's validity, burden sequence or the weight of religious exercise. Allowing the requested outsider obstruction would leave the affected person facing impassable or unreasonably difficult or hazardous access because of another person's religious choice. A violence-only rule leaves deliberate blockage untouched; later damages cannot restore a missed service. Nonobstructive prayer, counseling, signs, demonstrations and persuasion remain available. Notice, referral or a demand that the patient find another route does not preserve the same access in the affected encounter.

The parent/guardian exception removes penalties and every civil remedy, including preventive FACE injunctions, for the covered conduct directed exclusively at that person's own minor. This defeats any claim of universally overriding federal access enforcement. It does not, however, supply the asserted outsider exemption for obstruction directed at other service-seekers: the exclusive relationship and target, not supposed surviving civil FACE relief, supply the distinction. The dissent neither validates abuse nor presumes an equivalent state remedy. It reserves a genuinely qualifying parent/guardian application and makes no finding that a named plaintiff has or lacks that relationship in a different encounter.

The dissent retains the government's production and persuasion burden, assumes rather than finds substantial burden, and makes no finding about sincerity, exact acts, violence or prior guilt. Its position applies the governing test to the asserted access-denying immunity, not a categorical rule that medical access, commerce or third-party harm always defeats RFRA. Materially different nonobstructive practices, enforcement threats and accommodations remain for their own claims. Stevens, Ginsburg and Breyer join this common formulation of the assumed-obstruction ground; no distinct theory belonging to the Chief alone is incorporated. They otherwise support the judgments rejecting the presented constitutional and categorical damages challenges.

Authority and exact joins: [Public decision](../entering-law/PUBLIC_American_Life_League_v_Reno_merits_1995-11-13.md).

### A St P C v B C — 1995-11-20

Justice O'Connor dissents, joined by Scalia, Kennedy and Thomas. The dissent would reverse the categorical requirement of clear and convincing proof and remand for proper consideration of the protective procedure. Santosky concerned complete and irrevocable termination; here parental status survives, and treatment followed by a judicial best-interests determination permits supervised contact. Under Mathews, the process must be assessed as a whole, including danger to a child from an erroneous decision permitting renewed exposure. The severity or duration of a restriction demands adequate process but does not automatically import termination's proof burden.

The dissent distinguishes Foucha's expired confinement predicate and Heller's unjustified disparity between commitment classes. Neither supplies this new categorical rule. O'Connor's position preserves scrutiny of actual duration and adequate review; Scalia, Kennedy and Thomas likewise reject transferring a proof rule across distinct protective settings. All four recognize the serious contact loss and reject immediate reliance on the old finding entered without notice of these additional consequences. They do not validate every indefinite restriction, make periodic review a cure for every deprivation, find that abuse occurred, or direct enforcement on the defective notice premise. Their proposed reversal would leave those questions and lawful protective measures for further state proceedings.

Authority and exact joins: [Public decision](../entering-law/PUBLIC_A_St_P_C_v_B_C_merits_1995-11-20.md).

### Field v Mans — 1995-11-28

Justice Breyer dissents from Part II and the judgment, joined by Scalia; both join Part I's actual-and-justifiable-reliance rule. The disagreement concerns what the bankruptcy judge actually did with the record. The judge considered Field's continuing project visits, discussions of the development, the report that De Felice claimed ownership, opportunities for inquiry and the creditor's own circumstances. In the dissent's view, those recipient-specific circumstances and discovered warnings establish unjustifiability despite the judge's broader reasonable-person language. A remand would replace terminology without changing the dispositive application.

The dissent does not deny the affirmative finding of actual reliance. A person may in fact rely while failing the distinct justifiability limitation. Nor does it impose a universal obligation to search land records or consult an attorney, declare every incorrect legal label harmless, or resolve the obtained-by question. It would affirm because this record already supplies the correct-standard result; the separate causal issue would remain unnecessary to that disposition. The majority instead concludes that the explicit prudent-person formulation prevents treating the individualized discussion as a completed justifiability inquiry.

Authority and exact joins: [Public decision](../entering-law/PUBLIC_Field_v_Mans_merits_1995-11-28.md).

### Thompson v Keohane — 1995-11-29

Justice Thomas dissents. He would review the legal definition of custody independently but treat the concrete reasonable-person inference from the established circumstances as factual under §2254(d). Patton and Witt demonstrate that applying a legal standard does not itself turn the resulting judgment into a legal question. State judges must assess interacting circumstances and inferences; the absence of live testimony does not categorically remove the factual character of their task.

Thomas distinguishes Miller's particular history and function in independent voluntariness review from every antecedent warning question. National uniformity in the definition of custody does not, in his view, require independent redetermination of its every application. He would affirm the reviewed judgment on this classification ground while preserving the statute's factual exceptions. He does not make a new determination that Thompson was not in custody, adopt an alternative retroactivity bar, decide harmlessness or deny every habeas claim on an unpresented ground. The majority instead regards application of the arrest-equivalence boundary as a distinct constitutional task requiring independent review.

Authority and exact joins: [Public decision](../entering-law/PUBLIC_Thompson_v_Keohane_merits_1995-11-29.md).

### Things Remembered, Inc. v. Petrarca, No. 94-1530; 516 U.S. 124; October Term 1995.

**Kennedy, joined by Ginsburg, concurring.** They join the Court's opinion with the express understanding that the present covered-ground holding does not decide reviewability of a remand under Carnegie-Mellon University v. Cohill. Thermtron held both that a particular unauthorized remand was improper and that the ordinary review bar did not cover remands outside §1447(c). Cohill later recognized discretion to remand remaining state-law claims after elimination of the sole federal claim, despite the absence of express statutory authorization. Cohill did not decide whether §1447(d) bars review of that distinct remand. Neither today's affirmance nor these two Justices' reservation resolves that issue in either direction.

**Ginsburg, joined by Stevens, concurring.** They also find an independent review bar in §1452(b). Equity there means fairness or appropriateness, not the former division between legal and equitable pleading. Failure to remove promptly fits that meaning. Making a statutory time bar reviewable while equivalent delay labeled laches is immune would make appellate jurisdiction depend on a label. Hernandez v. Brakegate supplies the modern sense of equity; Sykes v. Texas Air explains the incoherence of label-dependent review. The chapter's structure and the 1977 House report's parallel treatment of remand review support a supplementary bankruptcy-remand regime, while Timbers directs attention to the coherent statutory scheme.

They give an alternative explanation as well: even if a procedural or jurisdictional impediment were called legal rather than equitable, equity may describe the choice to remand rather than dismiss. Section 1452(b) permits that fair disposition without requiring the impediment itself to fit an old equitable category. Their position concerns remands of claims related to bankruptcy. It does not insulate lack of subject-matter jurisdiction in a retained case: a decision not to remand may lack a separate immediate appeal while jurisdiction remains open to district-court reconsideration and eventual review through an otherwise proper channel. Their additional ground neither answers the separate Cohill question outside its statutory coverage nor commands a majority of the Court.

Authority: [Record](../entering-law/PUBLIC_Things_Remembered_Inc_v_Petrarca_merits_1995-12-05.md).

### Bailey v. United States; Robinson v. United States, Nos. 94-7448 and 94-7492; 516 U.S. 137; October Term 1995.

**Stone-Zsela, concurring in part and dissenting in part.** He joins the active-employment rule, its preservation of Smith's barter holding, the separate relation requirement, and reversal of both use-based appellate affirmances. Because the present convictions rest on the storage-and-accessibility use theory that the Court rejects, he would also vacate the firearm convictions now. He would then remand for ordinary proceedings, including any legally available charge based on carrying or possession that was properly preserved. That alternative does not convert possession into an offense under the applicable §924(c), disturb separate possession judgments, or decide an unpresented charging or retrial question. He requires neither automatic acquittal nor automatic retrial. No other Justice joins this different remedial position.

Authority: [Record](../entering-law/PUBLIC_Bailey_and_Robinson_v_United_States_merits_1995-12-06.md).

### Good News/Good Sports Club v. School District of Ladue; 28 F.3d 1501; Eighth Circuit No. 93-2148; no separate Supreme Court docket supplied.

**Kennedy, concurring in part and concurring in the judgment, joined by Scalia and Thomas.** All three join Parts I and III, including the actual-forum viewpoint rule, the concrete conclusion that the establishment defense fails on these private-use facts, and the remedial limits. They withhold assent from Part II's comprehensive contextual Lemon explanation. Their ground is the distinction between genuinely private religious advocacy and governmental religious action, reflected in Kennedy's Mergens opinion and in the access reasoning of Rosenberger and Chabad. Voluntary attendance, parental choice and private leadership support access here; a religious message or possible subjective impression of endorsement does not alone permit suppressing private expression. They propose no unlimited forum, general financing entitlement or alteration of existing establishment law through this concurrence.

**Stevens, dissenting.** Stevens would reverse the Eighth Circuit and leave the judgment for the school district in place. Perry and Cornelius permit a genuinely restricted forum, and his Mergens analysis treats the activity the school actually admitted as decisive. The Scout and athletic programs are secular activities related to the school's extracurricular program; the fact that both those programs and the adult-led Club concern moral development does not make them the same admitted activity. He acknowledges the policy's religious restriction and Lamb's Chapel's prohibition on viewpoint exclusion within an admitted subject, but finds the activity distinction sufficient for this Club's denial. The younger audience and continued extracurricular day reinforce the restricted character of the forum. His disagreement concerns that comparison, not a general exemption allowing schools to suppress religious viewpoints, a necessary finding that every Club meeting establishes religion, or rejection of Lamb's Chapel's governing rule.

Authority: [Record](../entering-law/PUBLIC_Good_News_Good_Sports_Club_v_School_District_of_Ladue_merits_1995-12-11.md).

### Love v. Pepersack; Fourth Circuit No. 94-1582, 47 F.3d 120; no separate Supreme Court docket supplied.

**O'Connor's Part II-B, joined by Scalia, Kennedy and Thomas — plurality ground supporting due-process affirmance.** The four assume the state interest and accept the alleged deliberate, knowing and malicious arrest-only practice. They nevertheless find this eligibility-screening restriction insufficient to establish the separate substantive wrong. Unresolved dispositions concern the program's eligibility subject even when officials knowingly exceed statutory authority. Collins separates state duty from constitutional arbitrariness; Romein and Beach supply limited economic-rights analogies. The four adopt no benign-motive finding or legislative-classification burden for this executive act. They reject categorical cure through state review, an absolute-discretion entitlement rule and a finding that deadline pressure compelled the policy. Their bounded conclusion does not exempt every affirmative licensing act. Stone-Zsela does not join this application; it is not the Court's controlling rationale.

**Stone-Zsela, concurring in part and dissenting in part.** The Chief Justice joins the common state-law/federal-wrong and contracting propositions and the personal-right, incorporation and necessary-acquisition holdings. He agrees with the due-process dismissal: unauthorized state administration does not by itself create a federal substantive wrong, state review corrected the state-law deprivation, and the incorporated Second Amendment supplies the specific protection for the asserted arms liberty. Substantive due process should not duplicate it. No separate entitlement to every lawful private transaction follows.

He would reverse the arms dismissal with constitutional infringement resolved, rather than vacate for an open application. In his view the guarantee centrally protects a law-abiding person's acquisition and keeping of a common firearm for lawful self-defense in the home. Nunn and Chandler support personal holders and defensive use while preserving regulation; Andrews supplies the acquisition incident, with its state-law and weapon-specific limits. Incorporation does not require reopening the Privileges or Immunities Clause.

His disqualification rule requires adjudicated conduct or incapacity genuinely connected to danger: conviction for a serious violent offense, a judicial dangerousness determination with adequate process, a domestic-violence protective order after notice and hearing, or adjudicated functional incapacity to possess safely. A bare diagnosis, accusation or uncontestable administrative label is insufficient. Convictions for murder, serious battery, armed robbery, violent domestic abuse, terrorism, planned unlawful force against government or comparable violence can support dispossession; arrests alone cannot. He does not settle every valid disqualifying conviction or restoration and duration rule.

On the pleaded record, Love's arrests were accusations; her identified obscene-show misdemeanor conviction established neither violence, dangerousness nor relevant incapacity. The Chief would hold that she could not constitutionally be denied an ordinary handgun solely because those arrests appeared in the files. The State may promptly investigate genuinely unresolved potentially disqualifying conduct under authority its law gives it. Missing dispositions do not become adjudications of guilt, and time pressure authorizes no judicially invented extra waiting period. Public safety does not supply a missing factual predicate.

His remand would resolve infringement while leaving personal responsibility, lawful relief and properly available defenses for ordinary proceedings. He decides no general public or concealed carrying rule, sensitive-place restriction, prohibited-weapon or magazine category, ordinary dealer licensing, recordkeeping, commercial regulation or storage rule. His affirmative application and adjudication-based disqualification framework receive no other Justice's join and are not the Court's law.

**Stevens, joined by Ginsburg and Breyer, and by Souter as to Part A only, concurring in part and dissenting in part.** All four join the procedural nonreach of immunity and the common state-law/federal-wrong and contracting propositions.

In **Part A**, all four would vacate due process and remand for assessment of the actual affirmative-policy claim. Zinermon and Stevens's Daniels concurrence distinguish substantive wrongdoing, complete when committed, from adequacy of procedure. Later correction alone cannot cure the former. The knowing-barrier allegations cannot be replaced by findings of necessary haste or official caution. Collins retains the need for a federal interest and substantive arbitrariness without completing this different application. An independent sufficient ground could permit affirmance despite erroneous reasoning, but these framing defects are material. The dissenters would return entitlement, constitutional sufficiency, attribution, defenses and relief for decision. They establish no violation, automatic discovery or trial, or damages entitlement. Malice and correction expense do not supply every element.

In **Part B**, Stevens, Ginsburg and Breyer would affirm arms dismissal under the specific state-nonapplication precedents. They acknowledge affirmative original evidence of individual keeping, acquisition and personal security, and the power to reconsider under Benton. Differing state clauses, military-suitable weapon boundaries, regulatory authority, the Reconstruction statute's equality and restoration setting, and Howard's privileges-or-immunities framing nevertheless fail, in their view, to justify this right-specific displacement of Cruikshank and Presser. Lewis's extant-felony setting is not a complete answer to Love. They adopt neither a collective-only rule, formal-enrollment condition nor state-correction cure. Souter does not join Part B; he joins the Court's arms holdings and bounded vacatur.

Authority: [Record](../entering-law/PUBLIC_Love_v_Pepersack_merits_1995-12-11.md).

### Southern Christian Leadership Conference of Alabama v. Sessions; 56 F.3d 1281; source petition identifier No. 95-647; no separate Supreme Court docket assigned.

**O'Connor, dissenting, joined by Kennedy.** They would affirm on the independently sufficient failure-of-proof ground under the governing Section 2 results inquiry. Houston Lawyers permits judicial-election coverage while retaining legitimate institutional considerations, and De Grandy requires proof of ultimate unequal opportunity rather than automatic liability from polarization or a feasible additional district. The trial court evaluated both experts, several kinds of elections, actual candidate preferences, party affiliation and incumbency. In their view the Court of Appeals upheld permissible contextual factfinding rather than applying a racial-intent requirement or numerical safe harbor. They agree that legal error would defeat factual deference, but find no error warranting reconsideration of this independent ground. They do not defend presumed racial partiality, categorical structural immunity, or the proposition that all proposed remedies are unconstitutional. Kennedy's earlier broader objection to judicial vote-dilution coverage is not the ground he selects here. Neither joins Thomas's noncoverage rationale.

**Thomas, dissenting, joined by Scalia.** They would affirm on their separate statutory view that Section 2 does not reach this judicial vote-dilution claim. Their preserved Holder and De Grandy positions reject dilution coverage; Scalia's Chisom and Houston Lawyers dissent supplies earlier judicial-election-specific support. They acknowledge that the Court's contrary coverage holdings govern unless changed, but continue to urge their construction rather than join the majority's comparison and totality framework. They do not join O'Connor's trial-record application merely because they seek the same decree. Their opinion supplies no additional votes for an evidentiary proposition, categorical remedial rule or present change in the Court's coverage law.

Authority: [Record](../entering-law/PUBLIC_Southern_Christian_Leadership_Conference_of_Alabama_v_Sessions_merits_1995-12-18.md).

### Lawrence v. Chater, No. 94-9323; 516 U.S. 163

**Stevens, concurring.** Stevens joins the Court's opinion and adds that certiorari administration properly permits a case-specific assessment of the totality of the circumstances. The value of obtaining the lower court's judgment about a potentially consequential development need not depend on first proving that the claimant will win. That discretion remains judicial and supplies no automatic rule accepting Government requests. No other Justice joins this supplemental explanation.

**Stone-Zsela, concurring in the judgment.** The Chief Justice would use §2106 when a material intervening development creates a reasonable possibility of a different result and reconsideration would conserve judicial resources. He does not adopt the Court's distinct reasonable-probability formulation. Henry separates this procedural return from a benefits award. The agency's changed position matters because it may unsettle the existing judgment, not because administrative deference supplies power to vacate. A strategic litigation reversal, an immaterial development, or a position outside lawful agency authority would not suffice, and remand may not predetermine the merits. Thomas Jefferson University and MCI supply cautions for the receiving court's independent examination of statutory authority, procedure, consistency, fair notice, and the position's lawful weight; they do not make the new position controlling. No other Justice joins this opinion.

**Scalia, dissenting, joined by Thomas.** The dissent would deny the petition. An intervening factor legally bearing on the decision, clarification needed to establish jurisdiction where Michigan v. Long does not govern, or a confession of error in the judgment can justify vacatur without a merits determination. An established defect can also support a justified error-correcting disposition; plenary review is not foreclosed. Conditional executive advocacy of uncertain relevance supplies no sufficient ground here. The agency's qualified acknowledgment establishes neither its legal force nor its application to this claimant. A clearly cognizable agency change could qualify, but a desire to reassess an arguably valid decision or obtain better reasoning does not. The unproved predicates of the state amendment do not cure that defect. The dissent concerns judicial justification for this remedy, not a ruling that the agency can never examine constitutional validity.

Authority: [Record](../entering-law/PUBLIC_Lawrence_v_Chater_GVR_1996-01-08.md).

### Stutson v. United States, No. 94-8988; 516 U.S. 193

**Stevens, concurring.** Stevens joins the Court and adds that case-specific, totality-of-the-circumstances discretion is a proper part of certiorari administration. The combination of an uncertain review premise and the potential loss of appellate consideration supports obtaining a fresh lower-court judgment without deciding excusability. This position creates no entitlement for every short delay and no exception to attribution of counsel's conduct. No other Justice joins this supplemental explanation.

**Scalia, dissenting, joined by Thomas.** The dissent would deny. Pioneer was available when the lower courts acted, and an unexplained affirmance may have applied its approach and still rejected the excuse. The Government concedes a point of law concerning relevance, not error in the judgment. Its changed argument therefore establishes neither new intervening law nor a defective judicial premise. The dissent accepts vacatur without a merits determination for an intervening factor legally bearing on the decision, clarification needed to establish jurisdiction where Michigan v. Long does not govern, or a confession of error in the judgment. It does not foreclose plenary review or a justified error-correcting disposition. None of those grounds is established here. Uncertainty about which ground sustained a judgment, or a desire for better reasoning, does not itself justify vacatur; the proper exercise of §2106 requires more than the possibility that reconsideration could change the result.

Authority: [Record](../entering-law/PUBLIC_Stutson_v_United_States_GVR_1996-01-08.md).

### Yamaha Motor Corp., U.S.A. v. Calhoun, No. 94-1387; 516 U.S. 199

No separate writing. Stone-Zsela's judgment-only agreement on Part I is stated in the opinion topology.

Authority: [Record](../entering-law/PUBLIC_Yamaha_Motor_Corp_USA_v_Calhoun_merits_1996-01-09.md).

### Allridge v. Scott; Fifth Circuit No. 93-9137; judgment below reported at 41 F.3d 213 (1994)

**Stone-Zsela, concurring in part and in the judgment.** The Chief Justice joins the parole-prediction holding, the admitted-mitigation ruling, and the bounded remand. A jury may not be told that a parole-eligible sentence legally excludes release. A fixed statutory minimum, if properly presented as a distinct claim, is a legal fact rather than a favorable prediction; that distinction establishes neither preservation nor retroactive entitlement here. He does not join the Court's independent Teague rationale or its additional rationale concerning unoffered medical evidence.

If a demonstrated, preserved denial of effective capital mitigation requires a separate harmless-error inquiry, he would extend the rationale of Brecht and O'Neal and require the State to establish beyond a reasonable doubt on the whole relevant record that the denial did not contribute to the death sentence. This is a proposed extension to a distinct category; those decisions do not already decide it. He does not find a violation, harmlessness, or a present right to a writ. Correction, if required, would be confined to punishment through adequate capital resentencing or a lawful noncapital sentence. The unintroduced medical evidence and separate chilling contention require their own lawful basis. No other Justice joins this proposal or opinion.

Authority: [Record](../entering-law/PUBLIC_Allridge_v_Scott_merits_1996-01-15.md).

### Lotus Development Corp. v. Borland International, Inc., No. 94-2003; 516 U.S. 233. — 1996-01-16

**O'Connor's plurality, joined by Kennedy, Thomas, and Ginsburg.** Section 102(b) leaves functions, procedures, and methods free, but an original selection and arrangement does not necessarily lose all protection merely because users employ it to operate software. Feist protects original arrangement while withholding ownership of the underlying material. Baker permits use of a system without establishing that every particular presentation of it is excluded. The plurality would reject the First Circuit's categorical treatment and distinguish any original expression from the unowned operation.

That view covers both implementations without declaring every command or all 469 choices protected. Compatibility matters to purpose and defenses, but does not automatically answer classification or fair use. Campbell requires the actual defense inquiry; Kennedy's caution against categorical borrowing permission remains consistent with the plurality's limits. The plurality supports remand, not automatic restoration of liability or an injunction, and does not reach code or screen claims outside the appeal.

**Stone-Zsela, concurring in the judgment.** He would protect the command compatibility necessary to operate users' existing macros through Campbell's full §107 inquiry. Such use has a concrete functional purpose beyond copying expression for its own sake; the commands' utilitarian character matters. The amount copied must be connected to actual interoperability rather than assumed necessary. Legally cognizable substitution and licensing markets count, while loss from lawful competition alone is not protected market harm. Commercial purpose is relevant but not decisive, and user investment creates no general property right in a learned interface.

The First Circuit did not resolve the fact-sensitive defenses. He would have it address them and obtain necessary findings, while allowing an alternative statutory ground within the grant without demanding an advisory copyrightability decision. He finds neither all compatibility copying fair nor all software structure unprotectable, and reserves source code, screen expression, and unnecessary copying. No other Justice joins this rationale.

**Souter, dissenting, joined by Scalia and Breyer.** The particular hierarchy is the method by which users issue executable instructions and existing macros operate. Section 102(b) excludes a method in whatever expressive form it is embodied; the availability of different original terms or arrangements does not remove that exclusion. Baker protects use of the system, and Feist distinguishes a copyright in the overall work from rights in excluded constituent material.

These are user commands, not the independent implementing code or separable visual presentation. That boundary answers the objection that treating all software as operational would swallow program protection. Because the copied subject matter is excluded, no fair-use decision is needed. The dissent would affirm both components without adopting a general interoperability license, Boudin's possible new privilege, or a rule denying protection to all interfaces.

Authority and exact joins: [Public source](../entering-law/PUBLIC_Lotus_v_Borland_merits_1996-01-16.md).

### Commissioner v. Lundy, No. 94-1785; 516 U.S. 235. — 1996-01-17

**Thomas, dissenting, joined by Stevens.** They would affirm consideration of the refund under the actual claim filed with the later return within three years of payment. In their reading, Congress created a hypothetical claim to protect taxpayers who had not made one; it did not direct courts to disregard a real, otherwise effective claim. The incorporated refund provisions can therefore operate through either the actual claim or the protective hypothetical. The majority's notice-date reading turns a benefit into an exclusive restriction without express language requiring that result.

This is a statutory disagreement, not an equitable exception. Dalm's timing conditions remain enforceable, and Williams supports using a remedy Congress actually provided. They would not require an actual claim in every Tax Court case, manufacture a return at the notice date, or give every delinquent filer a three-year window. Their ground concerns the real claim actually filed within three years of payment; the amount recoverable remains subject to ordinary computation.

Authority and exact joins: [Public source](../entering-law/PUBLIC_Commissioner_v_Lundy_merits_1996-01-17.md).

### Attwood v. Singletary, No. 95-6710; 516 U.S. 297. — 1996-01-22

**Stone-Zsela, concurring in the result.** He favors granting leave upon the established financial showing and promptly disposing of the present petition without attaching a disability to future litigation. In his view, equal access to federal process cannot be traded away merely for docket convenience; volume warrants efficient scrutiny of each paper, not a presumption that every unwritten claim is frivolous. Rule 39.8 permits a fee denial when justified but does not require that intermediate step before ordinary certiorari disposition.

His constitutional position seeks stronger protection against predictive, identity-based exclusion than the Court's record-specific ground establishes. His preference for direct screening is an institutional judgment, not an empirical finding about administrative cost. He preserves ordinary neutral rules, jurisdiction, sanctions for proved misconduct, and valid finality doctrines. No other Justice joins this explanation, and it does not turn denial of the petition into a ruling on the underlying claims.

Authority and exact joins: [Public source](../entering-law/PUBLIC_Attwood_v_Singletary_filing_and_certiorari_1996-01-22.md).

### Beadle v. City of Tampa; Eleventh Circuit No. 93-3271; 42 F.3d 633; no separate Supreme Court docket assigned. — 1996-02-05

**Stone-Zsela, dissenting.** He would affirm on the established training and assignment burdens while leaving the rejected release defense untouched. He agrees that neutral scheduling alone is insufficient and that Hardison requires accommodation unless the employer establishes hardship. In his view, the trial findings concern actual training exposure, work conditions, assignments, and the commitment to a later posting. Those operational burdens satisfy Hardison's existing threshold without a categorical public-safety exception.

He would consider an available arrangement that genuinely preserves the training objectives, but finds none established as one the City was legally required to adopt on this record. His position permits neither gratuitous refusal of workable alternatives nor automatic compliance through neutrality, and sets no universal staffing ratio or religious priority. His disagreement is with the majority's assessment of the existing hardship showing and resulting remand.

### United States v. Bishop; United States v. Stokes; Third Circuit Nos. 94-5321 and 94-5387; 66 F.3d 569. — 1996-02-05

**Stevens, concurring in part and dissenting in part, joined by no other Justice.** He joins the plea-reach, commerce, statutory-punishment, same-prosecution and both identification portions, as well as the independent physical-recording and evidentiary portions. His continuing objection to Hunter's foundation does not prevent application of that controlling decision to the expressly authorized punishment.

For the booking answer, Stevens distinguishes the officers' ability to ask about health from the prosecution's entitlement to use an unwarned substantive response. Innis's protection of express custodial questioning and the Quarles dissent's distinction between protective questioning and evidentiary use support excluding the accident assertion. His Muniz agreement concerning bodily performance and limited procedural communications does not make this factual account nontestimonial or require extension of its four-Justice administrative rationale. Davis's protection of meaningful custodial choice is consistent with that limit, although no counsel request is presented here. He accepts the genuine medical-purpose finding; his disagreement is with applying the booking exception to admit this answer, not with a supposed finding of pretext or a claim that the lower court used medical intent as its only test.

Stevens would vacate the appellate affirmance insofar as it sustains the answer and remand for the actual trial record's Chapman inquiry. The Government would have to establish beyond a reasonable doubt that the error did not contribute to each affected conviction. A count could stand if that burden is met; otherwise the lawful new-trial consequence would follow for the affected conviction. His position covers any recorded use only if the actual record shows it. It does not exclude separable physical observations, find an independent video defect, order an immediate new trial or acquittal, or reopen Bishop's plea.

**Stone-Zsela, concurring in part and dissenting in part, joined by no other Justice.** He joins application of Harris to both commerce claims and to Stokes's separate statutory and constitutional cumulative-punishment objections. He also joins admission of both eyewitness identification forms on the actual findings of independent recollection and reliability. He agrees with reaching Bishop's power-to-prosecute challenge without adding a threshold ground.

He would vacate the appellate disposition only as to Stokes's booking statement and booking videotape and remand those issues for proper findings. For the statement, the accepted medical purpose does not by itself answer Innis's objective inquiry into whether police should have known that questioning in the actual circumstances was reasonably likely to elicit an incriminating answer. For the video, the appellate account of reasons on both sides does not disclose enough of the relevance and unfair-prejudice analysis for him to reconstruct that assessment. He would require the lower court to complete those component-specific determinations, without treating an unreported transcript or absence of lengthy appellate discussion as a new finding about what the officers or trial court actually did.

Stone-Zsela does not now hold either item inadmissible. If the lower court finds improper admission, it must apply the appropriate constitutional or nonconstitutional prejudice inquiry and order the relief that inquiry requires. His remand preserves the distinction between an admissibility error and its effect; it supplies no finding of prejudice and no automatic new trial or acquittal. His proposed relief leaves the affirmed commerce, punishment and identification components, and Bishop's judgment, intact. He does not join Stevens's determination that admission of the answer was already erroneous.

Authority and exact joins: [Public source](../entering-law/PUBLIC_United_States_v_Bishop_and_Stokes_merits_1996-02-05.md).

### Sherman v. Community Consolidated School District 21 of Wheeling Township; Seventh Circuit No. 91-1684; 980 F.2d 437. No Supreme Court docket supplied. — 1996-02-12

**Kennedy, concurring in part and in the judgment, joined by Scalia and Thomas.** They join the concrete conclusion and limits in Parts I and III, but not Part II's comprehensive purpose, effect and entanglement explanation. Kennedy's Allegheny approach distinguishes a civic acknowledgment from governmental worship without requiring religious words to lose all meaning. The Pledge's actual civic character and protected right to decline assent support this result. The school remains the speaker; Good News's private-expression rationale therefore cannot itself sustain the program. Their agreement does not repudiate Lee, require a formal penalty before religious coercion can exist, or permit officials to add prayer merely because the activity is patriotic. They offer no broader holding through this concurrence.

**Chief Justice Stone-Zsela, dissenting.** He would reverse the establishment ruling and remand for prospective relief against the official religious component, limited to what is severable and necessary to redress these plaintiffs' injury. A school-selected declaration that the nation stands under God states a religious proposition for children's present affirmation. Its civic setting, brevity and history do not change who prescribes it or what it says. Lee's official-sponsorship principle therefore supplies the governing reason, although applying it here extends the rule beyond the clergy-led graduation prayer Lee decided. Silence answers compelled personal recitation; it does not answer sponsorship. Passing discussions of ceremonial references in earlier decisions do not settle this recurring elementary-school practice. Historical instruction may explain the Pledge and religious beliefs in earlier documents without requiring a current profession of them. His proposed relief preserves lawful patriotic exercises, genuinely private religious expression and references to religion in teaching; it would neither rewrite federal statutory wording nor depend on invented punishment, compulsory exit or individual psychological injury.

Authority and exact joins: [Public source](../entering-law/PUBLIC_Sherman_v_Community_Consolidated_School_District_21_merits_1996-02-12.md).

### United States v. Hale; Eighth Circuit No. 91-3830; 978 F.2d 1016; no Supreme Court docket supplied. — 1996-02-12

**Stone-Zsela, concurring in part and dissenting in part.** The Chief Justice joins the Court's bounded commerce analysis. Possession controls may prevent the defined restriction on new private machinegun stock and transfers from being defeated by an untraceable supply of newly made or unlawfully transferred weapons. The lawful-stock distinction helps identify that scheme. Lopez's commerce boundary remains; general crime costs and remote movement of an object would not supply this ground.

He also joins the governing personal-holder rule and the rejection of automatic military-utility immunity, but would affirm the §922(o) arms disposition. Love establishes a personal right; he does not treat that premise as an assumption. In his view, sustained automatic fire can be distinguished by its function and relationship to ordinary lawful civilian defense from an ordinary handgun. Military ancestry or appearance alone does not draw the line. Miller's discussion of military usefulness does not establish the claimed exemption. He would reject the claimed protection for the actual automatic weapons on that functional ground without deciding that every rifle, semiautomatic firearm, suppressor or specially regulated item is unprotected. This federal prosecution requires no incorporation decision.

He agrees with the judgments on the §5861(d) power challenge, the separate registration arms challenge, certificate admission, ordinary exclusion of the Senate excerpts, and refusal of judicial notice, adding no ground on those five components. His functional arms distinction receives no other Justice's join and does not become the Court's governing weapons rule.

**Scalia and Thomas, reservation accompanying their Part V joins.** Scalia and Thomas join this bounded application without abandoning their White reservation concerning possible reconsideration of formalized testimonial materials. Their join adopts neither a new categorical test nor a rule excluding formal prosecutorial affidavits from confrontation.

Authority and exact joins: [Public source](../entering-law/PUBLIC_United_States_v_Hale_merits_1996-02-12.md).

### Behrens v. Pelletier; No. 94-1244. — 1996-02-21

**Breyer, concurring in part and dissenting in part, joined by Stevens.** They would affirm the jurisdictional dismissal. They join Parts II and III's conditional legal/factual and claim-specific rules but find no authorization for a second ordinary pretrial appeal as of right. Cohen and Coopers & Lybrand require attention to importance and practical finality, not merely identification of another separable legal question. One pretrial immunity appeal adequately protects the sufficiently important interest in avoiding trial; repeated appeals can duplicate legal adjudication and delay resolution, while avoidance of additional discovery does not necessarily warrant another interruption. The reinstated termination claim presents a substantial argument for additional review, but does not justify expanding judge-made collateral review in this case. Mitchell's immunity-from-suit rationale does not require an appeal at each successive stage.

They would leave an exceptional later legal question to a separately authorized route. Section 1292(b) requires the District Judge's written statement that the order involves a controlling legal question, substantial ground for difference of opinion, and that immediate appeal may materially advance the litigation's termination. Application must be made within ten days, and the Court of Appeals may permit review in its discretion; applying alone creates no stay. No such certification or permission is established here. Sections 1292(e) and 2072(c) authorize rulemaking within §2072's substantive-rights limit; they are not themselves an operative rule permitting this appeal. The dissent favors that institutional route over another appeal as of right. It neither determines that every issue Behrens raises is factual nor decides his immunity.

Authority and exact joins: [Public source](../entering-law/PUBLIC_Behrens_v_Pelletier_merits_1996-02-21.md).

### Peacock v. Thomas, No. 94-1453 — February 21, 1996

Stevens dissents from jurisdictional dismissal. A court's continuing authority to effectuate its judgment, he concludes, permits consideration of restoration when a person controlling the debtor deliberately diverts its assets to defeat collection. Wayman, Riggs and Labette County support that enforcement function; Beecher's attempted addition of independently liable persons does not resolve this distinct interference with execution. But the full corporate debt cannot simply be imposed on Peacock. Stevens would vacate the unqualified liability and derivative-fee affirmance and remand to determine whether restorative relief remains legally and procedurally available. The existing findings do not establish a ready-made asset award, that every transfer occurred after judgment, that Peacock received every asset, or a particular recoverable value. State enforcement law ordinarily supplies the Rule 69 rule; federal uniformity alone does not justify displacement. The preserved personal-jurisdiction and service objections must be resolved before renewed personal relief, and any fee or expense assessment requires its own lawful basis. He reserves the alternative ERISA cause and would not direct immediate payment, reinstate a rejected count or guarantee recovery. The original Tru-Tech judgment remains undisturbed under his approach as well.

### Jones v. ABC-TV, No. 95-7186 — February 26, 1996

Stone-Zsela concurs in the financial and current-paper treatment and agrees that the prospective condition should be refused. He would require individual consideration of future ordinary civil-certiorari submissions by an otherwise financially eligible litigant. Rule 39.8 addresses a frivolous or malicious submission; past abuse does not establish the contents of an unwritten petition. Automatic fee denial based on identity and history risks excluding a later legitimate claim solely because its author cannot pay. Inherent docket authority should implement the Rules' current-paper inquiry, while permitting prompt rejection of a submission actually shown defective.

His position goes beyond the Court's record-specific ground. It concerns ordinary civil-certiorari fee treatment, does not decide every extraordinary-writ restriction, vacate unreviewed orders or establish unlimited fee-free litigation in every court, and preserves jurisdictional, timeliness, form and current-paper controls. Individual consideration requires no merits opinion, hearing or elaborate explanation for every filing. Financial eligibility must still be established; once it is established and current frivolousness or malice is not shown, he would grant financial leave and consider certiorari separately. The missing financial proof is not itself ineligibility, and the pending treatment grants neither review nor relief against the respondents.

Authority and exact joins: [Public decision](../entering-law/PUBLIC_Jones_v_ABC_TV_filing_order_1996-02-26.md).



### Matsushita Electric Industrial Co. v. Epstein, No. 94-1809 — February 27, 1996

**Stone-Zsela, concurring.** The Chief Justice joins reversal, ordinary Delaware recognition, the §27 holding, and the constitutional minimum and unresolved case application. He would give the judgment the effect §1738 requires unless respondents establish a fundamental defect in jurisdiction, notice, representation or binding operation. Hansberry and Shutts permit collateral attack where constitutionally deficient notice, a disabling conflict, collusion, or representation tantamount to no representation deprived absent members of a genuine adversarial representative. Ordinary disagreement with strategy, valuation or settlement terms does not establish that structural failure. Exclusive federal jurisdiction bars state adjudication of the federal cause, but not its settlement through a judgment the State was competent to enter. He therefore does not join the Court's complete reservation of the collateral-attack standard. He finds neither actual adequacy nor inadequacy here and supports the remand within those limits. No other Justice joins this complete standard.

**Ginsburg, concurring in part and dissenting in part.** Ginsburg and Stevens would vacate and remand for the lower federal courts to determine Delaware preclusive effect in the first instance, without affirming the Ninth Circuit's overbroad federal rule. They accept the judgment's incorporated release but would first examine Nottingham's identical-factual-predicate limit, Prezant's representative requirements and the judgment's finality. General state power to approve releases does not settle that application. Ginsburg additionally reserves the further §27 exception question until the state-effect predicate is established; Stevens does not share that reservation and joins the Court's nonrepeal holding.

In the representation discussion, joined by Stevens and Souter, Ginsburg explains that constitutionally adequate representation must exist throughout the litigation and that a final class judgment remains susceptible to a legally proper collateral challenge for failure of that prerequisite. Notice and opt-outs are distinct protections. Hansberry, Shutts and Prezant support attention to actual representative authority and interests. The existing findings and hearing do not establish the absence of a possible constitutional objection; neither do the objections prove failure. Respondents' inadequacy contention and petitioners' response that the issue was fully and fairly litigated both remain open. Souter joins this explanation while supporting ordinary Delaware recognition and reversal; he does not join the first-instance state-law remand or Ginsburg's §27 reservation.

Authority and exact joins: [Public decision](../entering-law/PUBLIC_Matsushita_Electric_Industrial_Co_v_Epstein_merits_1996-02-27.md).



### Hercules, Inc. v. United States, No. 94-818; 516 U.S. 417 — March 4, 1996

**Breyer, dissenting, joined throughout by O'Connor.** They would vacate the judgment in part and remand both petitioners' preserved specifications-warranty claims, including settlement and tort-defense expenses, and Thompson's contextual implied-in-fact indemnity claim. Other disposed claims would remain undisturbed.

In Part I, they read Spearin, Ryan, Weyerhaeuser and Hatzlachh as permitting inquiry into whether an actual authorized contractual undertaking included foreseeable third-party consequences. They reject the Federal Circuit's categorical equation between a successful warranty claim and a certainly successful government-contractor defense. The 1984 settlement cannot be assessed simply as though later defense rulings had already assured victory; defending even successfully can leave expenses. Kania's distinct nonprosecution and remote-expense setting does not settle procurement consequential damages. The actual duty, breach, causal connection, foreseeability, ex ante litigation risk, reasonableness and allocation must be examined to the extent necessary and procedurally available. Neither settlement approval nor government specifications prove those elements.

In Part II, they agree that §707 alone promises no reimbursement but would allow Thompson to attempt to prove an authorized implied-in-fact undertaking from the circumstances considered together. Compulsion, specifications, alleged control and knowledge, and the surrounding liability protection may inform the bargain actually made. Sutton still requires authority. An obligation imposed solely for fairness would fail, and neither the existence of special contracting authority nor a judicial label proves approval. They infer no indemnity cap or insurer-equivalent amount.

Part III limits the remedy to the preserved contract claims requiring further adjudication. The Government retains its available legal and factual defenses. Missing documents alone guarantee neither discovery nor trial; no promise, breach, payment entitlement or damages amount is found. The dissent does not revive Hercules's separate indemnity claim, adjudicate an independent takings or superior-knowledge cause, or award fees for this contract litigation. Its proposed remand and causation analysis are noncontrolling.

Authority and exact joins: [Public decision](../entering-law/PUBLIC_Hercules_Inc_v_United_States_merits_1996-03-04.md).



### Bennis v. Michigan, No. 94-8729; 516 U.S. 442 — March 4, 1996

**O'Connor, dissenting, joined by Scalia, Thomas and Ginsburg.** The dissent would affirm the Michigan judgment on the reviewed due-process and takings objections. Goldsmith-Grant, Van Oster and Calero-Toledo sustain forfeiture despite ignorance where the owner voluntarily made property available and it was actually used unlawfully. Here the car both transported the participants and provided the place of the act; this is not a decision about a remote, fortuitous association with crime. Assumed lack of knowledge does not establish the additional reasonable-prevention category, and Calero-Toledo's reservation does not require its adoption as a new ground for remand.

Austin's treatment of punitive forfeiture, Buena Vista's enacted defense and Good's seizure-process protection do not already create the constitutional immunity sought. The dissent preserves those actual limits, statutory authority and constitutionally required process. It does not find that Tina omitted an available precaution, decide a proven all-reasonable-prevention case, or authorize forfeiture of every property loosely associated with wrongdoing. Because it sustains this forfeiture, the separate compensation claim fails; neither an invalid forfeiture nor every governmental acquisition is thereby exempted from constitutional scrutiny.

**Thomas, dissenting separately and joining O'Connor.** Settled entrusted-property forfeiture supports affirmance, but the absence of a personal-fault requirement makes historical limits on what counts as an instrumentality especially important. A government may not make those limits disappear simply by calling property a nuisance. This car's admitted transport and use provide a sufficient basis for applying Van Oster without relying on an instrumentality concession. Thomas does not establish a comprehensive nexus test, adopt Scalia's earlier exclusive excessiveness formula or characterize every historical forfeiture as personal punishment. Possible remedial costs do not supply a finding that this forfeiture was exclusively remedial or constitutionally costless to Tina.

**Ginsburg, dissenting separately and joining O'Connor.** The voluntary sharing of a jointly owned vehicle and actual equitable consideration distinguish this application from an unrestricted power to punish innocent third parties. The trial court considered alternatives; the qualitative cost concern and reference to another family automobile supply no verified expense calculation or finding of substitute transportation. She would apply the inherited entrustment rule to assumed ignorance here, while reserving the materially different owner who proves all reasonably expected prevention and different exorbitant applications.

A hearing does not cure every substantive constitutional defect, and low property value does not erase an owner's rights. Equitable discretion is material context, not a mandatory federal offset or an answer if constitutionally required owner protection is established. Her conclusion rests on the existing forfeiture rule in this setting, without a precise ownership fraction, an unverified concession about the vehicle or a newly found valuation.

Authority and exact joins: [Public decision](../entering-law/PUBLIC_Bennis_v_Michigan_merits_1996-03-04.md).



### Action for Children’s Television and Pacifica Foundation v. FCC — March 4, 1996

**Souter, concurring in part and dissenting in part.** Souter joins the content-based standard, independent review and Pacifica's continued limits. He would vacate approval of the actual schedule for renewed examination of its boundary, contextual reach, practical adult opportunities and alternatives. The lower majority did address 10 p.m. by reasoning from its midnight conclusion and removing unequal treatment; he finds that analysis insufficiently focused, not wholly absent. Turner supports a careful remand without turning present uncertainty into final constitutional invalidity. Actual evidence exists, and further analysis may show adequate support or require relief. He therefore withholds assent to final invalidity and mandatory removal, preserves nighttime protection, and prescribes neither a new agency hearing nor automatic interim relief. Section 551 alone requires no remand, and future equipment is no present factual premise.

**Stevens, dissenting, joined by Scalia and Breyer.** The dissent would affirm the actual uniform decree under demanding review. Pacifica permits contextual broadcast channeling; Sable's rejection of wholesale adult exclusion does not establish an effective telephone-like means of segregating this audience. Substantial child access, rapid tuning, multiple receivers, the meaningful 10 p.m. harbor and evidence-sensitive contextual defenses together justify this schedule. The dissent accepts protected adult speech and independent review, but finds the majority gives insufficient weight to the remaining opportunities and the practical difficulty of protecting children without timed channeling. It requires neither a formal legislative report nor scientific certainty, makes no finding that every program harms children, and adopts no general lower-value hierarchy. No foolproof-alternative condition, operational V-chip or automatic station-rating exemption supplies its conclusion. Its proposed affirmance preserves the favorable nighttime protection, actual defenses and properly supported future challenges.

### Varity Corp. v. Howe, No. 94-1471; 516 U.S. 489 — March 19, 1996

**Stone-Zsela, concurring in part and in the judgment.** He joins the holdings on fiduciary administration and deliberate loyalty breach. Varity used its administrative role to explain existing benefit security and induce surrender through materially false assurances; employer restructuring powers do not excuse that separate function. He would permit individual equitable redress only when no other ERISA provision adequately remedies the same injury. Sections 502(a)(1)(B)–(3) must retain their separate tasks, and Russell's reserved question permits the express equitable action without weakening Mertens's prohibition on converting it into general legal damages. He therefore supports the class's source-bound restoration while excluding legal or punitive damages and duplicate relief through another adequate statutory channel. His condition is stronger than the Court's statement that adequate statutory relief normally makes further equity inappropriate; he does not join Part III. He concurs in affirmance of the ten retirees' distinct assignment component without adding a ground and does not join Part IV. He supplies no finding that they voluntarily left their plan, no categorical denial of a benefits action and no new classification of the monetary items.

**Thomas, dissenting, joined by O'Connor and Scalia.** The dissent reads §§409 and 502(a)(2) as the specific statutory route for fiduciary-breach relief, with recovery directed to the plan. In its view, §502(a)(3)'s residual language cannot remove that deliberate recipient limitation for the same violation; the provision still applies to other statutory and plan obligations. Russell expressly reserved this question, but its respect for ERISA's differentiated enforcement structure supports that construction. Actual Mertens decided the remedy category and reserved its antecedent action question, so it supplies no prior action bar. The dissent reaches its construction independently rather than treating either precedent as already dispositive.

The dissent also rejects the class's fiduciary-capacity theory. Accurate descriptions of current benefit terms do not, in its view, turn corporate viability forecasts into discretionary administration merely because the employer also administers a plan. It accepts the findings of deliberate deception but disputes their ERISA classification; participant understanding and general fiduciary status cannot replace the statutory function. This ground does not dispose of the ten retirees' different assignment claim. Assuming their undisturbed breach, the dissent applies its individual-action objection to both groups. Reserved amendment power does not establish a valid assignment or erase the findings. It would reverse the reviewed fiduciary-breach recovery and remand for any preserved §510 or estoppel ground, without guaranteeing recovery, dismissing the entire action, reviving closed claims or deciding the unpresented monetary classifications.

### Ayers v. Fordice — March 25, 1996

**Stone-Zsela, dissenting.** The Chief Justice would vacate only the additional-library-relief denial. When an established segregation-caused educational injury remains unremedied, the absence of predicted additional white enrollment cannot by itself justify refusing necessary, practicable and educationally sound repair. Fordice places the dismantlement burden on the State and requires examination of interacting inherited policies. Jenkins recognizes educational repair as an independently sufficient ground; Milliken II connects educational remedies beyond pupil assignment to the violation. Its application to university libraries develops the doctrine; Milliken II did not decide this question.

The district court attributed collection differences to historical missions and denied enlargement beyond them because the holdings were not shown to preclude the institutions as viable choices for white students. It also credited Jackson State and Alcorn expansions. The dissent preserves supported findings, including those about volume counts and student choice, but finds the educational-repair inquiry unresolved. Different lawful missions may require different collections. Inherited missions cannot conclusively justify resource limits when mission policies continue fostering separation and library allocations are traceable to the extent they follow those missions.

Reconsideration would ask whether a library condition attributable to the dual system remains unremedied, what resources are needed for each institution's legally justified mission—including the program changes already ordered in decree paragraphs 3–10—and what practicable, educationally sound repair remains necessary after crediting the existing improvements. Neither traceability, historical inadequacy nor a collection disparity itself establishes a present injury or a necessary expenditure. If the libraries adequately support lawful missions and existing improvements remedy any attributable injury, no additional relief follows.

The proposed remand preserves existing findings and leaves all other decree provisions and appellate challenges undisturbed without merits affirmance. It reopens no mission, program, admissions or equipment determination and adjudicates no scholarship or endowment eligibility, committee procedure, maintenance control or reporting deadline. It requires neither identical collections nor funding parity, a fixed appropriation, new hearing, universal proof protocol or withdrawal of supervision. Historically black institutions are not themselves the constitutional wrong. Any release question retains Freeman's and Jenkins's distinct requirements.

Authority and exact joins: [Public decision](../entering-law/PUBLIC_Ayers_v_Fordice_certiorari_before_judgment_1996-03-25.md).
